column1: # Game profile of LEGO® Harry Potter™ Collection (010052A00B5D2000), update 1.0.2 (v131072), SDK 5.4.0.
# Format: see dm/games/README.md
# TT Games' own renderer: the Windows D3D11 DLLs ported to nn::ro modules. main is 750 instructions that mount the
# RomFS; libHarryLauncher.nro (nro2) starts and loads libharry1.nro (nro1, Years 1-4) or libharry2.nro (nro0,
# Years 5-7) as a module — lhp_switch_dll_launcher.nrr registers all three. Modules main, sdk and those three NROs
# are rewritten, and the host maps the NROs at start (loader.c, "NRO modules").
# Years 5-7's frame is built by three routines this build does not order as the console does, and that is the crash
# this profile's one cut fixes: the recorder stores a pass's record in the live table at singleton+0x9d0
# (nro0+0xd2ff0), the begin-frame routine copies the 24 entries into the published table at singleton+0xa90 a frame
# phase later (nro0+0x15f420), and the replay reads the published table in the same frame (nro0+0xd39c0 and eleven
# other sites) — different threads, two locks that do not order them. patches.py publishes the record at the store
# (nro0+0xd3138); dm/host/hle_nullpass.c reads a load that still faults in the null page as zero for the sites a
# frame reaches before it fills them (the emulator's recovery, natively).
# What this profile does NOT hold: the shader tables. They are the build's own output (the derived profile), and 493
# of the map's rows come from a run-time dump no split reproduces (docs/reference/shaders.md, "Shaders whose bytes
# exist only in a run-time dump"). The note says where they are and what each count is.

column1: # ---- Present path (Years 5-7: the configuration the user called "really really improved", MetalFX removed) ----
# 1920x1080 -> 5120x2880 drawable in a fullscreen window, bilinear present, and a 4-deep ring of present
# snapshots: every present is copied into a host texture of its own, so the guest's next frame cannot overwrite the
# texture the screen is showing. At a fixed 2560x1440 drawable, per 100 presents: bilinear with no ring 15.58,
# bilinear with ring 4 1.68, MetalFX with ring 4 0.00 — and real GPU serialisation on the first (DM_NVN_PASSGPU_SERIAL)
# leaves it at 15.00, so the present path is the carrier and GPU load is not. The drawable is not a shippable knob:
# only the fullscreen window reaches 5120x2880 (front_mac.m consults DM_FULLSCREEN, never a size).
# present_upscale is off: MetalFX's 0.00 was a measurement, not an absence — its spatial scaler anti-aliases the
# glyph edges, so the residual lattice reads nbrh ~39.5 with white under the 0.06 companion line, and it costs GPU
# time every frame (orch/nometalfx/REPORT.md, the windowed 2560x1440 arm with the detector at nbrh>=30).
# ui_republish stays 0. The republish copies the guest's 5 MB UI staging array over the pool block its draws name
# three times a frame, after the frame produced it and with no ordering against a GPU holding 2 submissions in
# flight; at this configuration it does no work the draws can see (its flagged population is identical to OFF) and
# put the glyph wall back at 8.90 per 100 in one of two ON runs (OFF: 1.70 and 1.60; ON: 1.66 and 1.66).
# These four are also pinned as environment variables in the bundle's env.txt: the app's settings window exports
# its own defaults (Upscaling=Standard, Window, Frame buffering off) over this compiled profile, so the bundle
# carries both.
fullscreen
present_upscale
present_snap
ui_republish
